Hi Monica,

Thanks for running the initial sizing conversation last week. Procurement asked us to get a little deeper before we move forward with a commitment: they want a SKU-fitment workbook that maps our expected workload (mix of chat + embeddings pipelines, 75%/25%) to recommended reserved SKUs, with two throughput targets — sustained (90th percentile) and burst — and an explicit fallback plan if a preferred GPU family is constrained.

Can Redwood provide:
- A completed workbook with per-SKU throughput (tokens/sec & concurrency) for our two workload buckets
- A short note on how quantization/kv-caching assumptions affect throughput numbers
- A proposed canary/rollout phasing (what to reserve first vs. later)

We're aiming to finalize the first-phase commitment by the end of June. I've attached AstraTech_RFI_SKU_Workbook_v1.xlsx with our sample traces and a notional QPS profile.

Appreciate a short response with next steps and an ETA.

Lina — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the traces. I've started filling the workbook and attached our initial set of notes (Redwood_Sku_Fitment_Notes.pdf). High-level callouts up front:

1) Preferred SKU families: for your mix (chat-heavy + embeddings) we recommend a blend of A100-80GB quantized instances for embeddings-heavy workers and H100-80GB for chat inference (low-latency).
2) Throughput assumptions: workbook sheets A/B use your traces and two run modes (sustained 90th pct, and burst 5-min peaks). We include tokens/sec and concurrent request limits per slot.
3) Fallbacks: we model two fallback lanes — (1) mixed-quantized variants on A100 if H100 capacity is constrained, (2) model-split: embeddings on cheaper quantized A100s while keeping chat on H100s.

ETA: we'll finish the workbook with calibrated throughput numbers and a phasing proposal by COB Wednesday (2026-06-03). If procurement wants a live walkthrough, propose Thu 06/04 for a 45-min session.

I'll pull Karthik in for pricing sensitivity and Ben to confirm SLA/fallback pricing impacts.

Adding a few technical validation points from my side so the workbook's numbers line up with procurement expectations:

- For the 90th percentile sustained numbers we used a 2% request drop tolerance and enabled prefix KV caching for chat sessions (saves ~20-30% tokens/sec for repeated prompts). We should call this out explicitly in the workbook assumptions tab.
- Quantization: INT8 profiles were benchmarked; INT4 shows gains but increases token error-rate risk for chat — we recommend keeping chat on INT8 unless AstraTech is comfortable with eval-driven regressions.
- Concurrency planning: we recommend reserving a 15% burst buffer beyond projected 95th pct concurrency to avoid throttle events during rollout.

I'll be available to join the walkthrough. Also, one open question: does AstraTech want us to map reserved SKUs to a month-by-month phasing (i.e., reserve a small H100 pool month 1, then expand)? I recommend a two-phase approach: baseline (embeddings + low-latency chat) then scale chat capacity in month 2 if SLA metrics are met.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Lina — following the workshop and procurement feedback, attached is the finalized workbook and short executive summary. Highlights:

- Recommended two-phase reserve: Month 0 (20% baseline reserved: 8x H100-equivalent slots for chat + 12x A100 quantized slots for embeddings), Month 1-3 gradual scale to target (40% reserved) contingent on 30-day SLA meters.
- Modeled fallback costs: A100 quantized fallback increases monthly spend by ~27% under a 30% fallback load; model-split fallback increases ops complexity but keeps incremental cost to ~12%. See the risk matrix sheet for tradeoffs to latency and quality.
- Assumptions tab: explicit KV caching hit-rates (20%-30%), INT8 quality delta guidance, concurrency headroom (+15%) included.

Next steps: procurement to confirm final sizing and preferred fallback lane (A100 quantized vs model-split) by 2026-06-12 so we can lock month-1 SKUs.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a follow-up call if you want to review the workbook line-by-line.
